title: a negated Token condition is always false because Token instances are truthy

ground_truth.statement: PHP has no userland __toBool(), and instances of the final user-defined class Token are truthy. Thus `!$token` is false for every permitted argument: the branch returning true is dead and is_falsy() always returns false. This does not claim that internal objects with custom bool casts are always truthy.

notes: The fixture uses a final user-defined class. Some internal objects, such as GMP zero, can cast to false; they are outside this function's input domain. All three tools report the dead branch; Psalm words it as 'Type Token for $token is never falsy'.
